nodes.name: Vector norms
nodes.statement: For a vector $v\in \mathbb{R}^p$, let $\|v\|_{2}:=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{p}|v_i|^2}$ be the Euclidean norm, $\|v\|_{1}:=\sum_{i=1}^{p}|v_i|$ be the $\ell^1$ norm, and $\|v\|_\infty:=\max|v_i|$ be the $\ell^\infty$ norm.
nodes.statement_short: Euclidean, $\ell^1$ and $\ell^\infty$ norms of a vector.

nodes.name: Euclidean inner product
nodes.statement: Let $\left<x, x'\right>:=\sum_{i=1}^{p}x_{i}x_{i}'$ be the Euclidean inner product in $\mathbb{R}^p$.

nodes.name: Matrix entry notation
nodes.statement: For a matrix $M\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$, let $M_{i,j}$ denote the $(i,j)$ element of $M$.

nodes.name: Operator and Frobenius norms
nodes.statement: Let $\|M\|_{\text{op}}:=\sup_{\|x\|_2=1} \|Mx\|_{2}$ be the operator norm, and let $\|M\|_{F}:= \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{k} |M_{i,j}|^{2}}$ be the Frobenius norm.

nodes.name: Identity matrix
nodes.statement: Let $I$ be the $n\times n$ identity matrix.

nodes.name: Centering matrix
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{1}\in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be the vector of all $1$s, and let $C= I-n^{-1} \mathbf{1} \mathbf{1}^{\top}$ be the centering matrix.

nodes.name: Two-class training data
nodes.statement: Let $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$ be independent pairs, where $x_i\in \mathbb{R}^p$ is the vector of features, and $y_i\in \mathbb{R}^2$ is the indicator of class membership such that $y_{ik} = 1$ if $i$th sample belongs to class $k$, $i\in C_k$, and $y_{ik} = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.section: 2.1 Linear Discriminant Analysis and Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: Independent feature/label pairs with one-hot class indicators $y_i\in\mathbb{R}^2$.

nodes.name: Class sample sizes
nodes.statement: Let $n_1$ and $n_2$ denote the number of samples in each respective class so that $n = n_1 + n_2$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Linear Discriminant Analysis and Optimal Scoring

nodes.name: Feature and indicator matrices
nodes.statement: Let $X\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$ and $Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times 2}$ denote the corresponding feature and indicator matrices, and without loss of generality let $X$ be column-centered.
nodes.section: 2.1 Linear Discriminant Analysis and Optimal Scoring

nodes.name: Optimal scoring problem
nodes.statement: The optimal scoring problem \cite{Hastie:1994cx} finds the discriminant vector $\beta \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and the scores vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^2$ by solving \begin{align} \begin{split} &\mathrm{minimize}_{\theta, \beta}\|Y\theta-X\beta\|_{2}^{2}\\ &\text{subject to }n^{-1}\theta^{\top}Y^{\top}Y\theta=1,\,\theta^{\top}Y^{\top}Y \mathbf{1}=0. \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.section: 2.1 Linear Discriminant Analysis and Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: Jointly choose class scores $\theta$ and discriminant vector $\beta$ minimizing $\|Y\theta-X\beta\|^2$ under normalization constraints.

nodes.name: Optimal scoring reduces to linear regression
nodes.statement: Since the solution vector of scores has explicit form up to a sign, $\widehat \theta = (\sqrt{n_2/n_1}\ -\sqrt{n_1/n_2})^{\top}$, ~\eqref{eq:OptScoring} is equivalent to the linear regression problem \begin{equation} \mathrm{minimize}_{\beta}\|Y\widehat \theta - X\beta\|_2^2. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.1 Linear Discriminant Analysis and Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: Optimal scores are explicit, $\widehat\theta=(\sqrt{n_2/n_1},-\sqrt{n_1/n_2})^\top$, so optimal scoring is a least-squares regression in $\beta$.

nodes.name: Optimal scoring recovers the LDA direction
nodes.statement: The solution $\widehat \beta$ corresponds to the discriminant vector in LDA up to scaling \cite[Section 3.4]{hastie_penalized_1995}. Thus, linear discriminant analysis can be reduced to finding the solution to problem~\eqref{eq:optReg}.
nodes.section: 2.1 Linear Discriminant Analysis and Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: The optimal-scoring solution is the LDA discriminant direction up to scale, so LDA reduces to problem (2).

nodes.name: RKHS feature map and kernel
nodes.statement: The data is mapped into a RKHS $\mathcal{H}$ via $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{p}\to \mathcal{H}$ with an accompanying kernel $k:\mathbb{R}^{p}\times \mathbb{R}^{p}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $\left<\Phi(x),\Phi(x')\right>_{\mathcal{H}}=k(x,x')$ for any $x, x' \in \mathbb{R}^{p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Data mapped by $\Phi$ into an RKHS $\mathcal{H}$ whose inner product is given by the kernel $k$.

nodes.name: RKHS norm
nodes.statement: We let $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{H}}$ be the norm induced by the inner product $\left<\cdot\,,\,\cdot\right>_\mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: Reproducing property
nodes.statement: By the \emph{reproducing property} of $\mathcal{H}$: $\left<\Phi(x), f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}=f(x)$ for all $x\in \mathbb{R}^{p}$ and $f\in \mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: Kernelization
nodes.statement: Thus, any classifier that relies on the training data only through the inner products can be \emph{kernelized} by substituting kernel evaluations in place of inner products.

nodes.name: Gaussian, polynomial and sigmoid kernels
nodes.statement: Some commonly-used kernels are the gaussian kernel $k(x,x')=\exp(-\sigma^{-2} \|x-x'\|_{2}^2)$ with $\sigma >0$, the polynomial kernel $k(x,x')= (1+\left<x, x'\right>)^{d}$ with $d$ a positive integer, and the sigmoid kernel $k(x,x')=\tanh(c\left<x, x'\right>+t)$ with $c>0$, $t\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian $\exp(-\|x-x'\|^2/\sigma^2)$, polynomial $(1+\langle x,x'\rangle)^d$ and sigmoid $\tanh(c\langle x,x'\rangle+t)$ kernels.

nodes.name: Kernel matrix
nodes.statement: We let $\mathbf{K}\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ denote the kernel matrix $\mathbf{K}_{i,j}:=k(x_i, x_j)$ based on observed feature vectors $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^n$.

nodes.name: Discriminant function
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be the discriminant function in $\mathcal{H}$ with corresponding map $\Phi$ and kernel $k$.

nodes.name: Centered feature map
nodes.statement: We substitute each inner product $x_i^{\top}\beta = \langle x_i, \beta \rangle$ with inner product in $\mathcal{H}$, $\langle \Phi(x_i) - \overline{\Phi}, f \rangle_{\mathcal{H}}$, where we apply centering to $\Phi(x_i)$ via $\overline{\Phi}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Phi(x_i)$ to take into account column-centering of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $x_i^\top\beta$ by $\langle\Phi(x_i)-\overline\Phi,f\rangle_{\mathcal{H}}$ with $\overline\Phi$ the mean feature map.

nodes.name: Optimal scoring problem in the RKHS
nodes.statement: The corresponding optimal scoring problem in $\mathcal{H}$ takes the form \begin{equation*} \mathrm{minimize}_{ f\in \mathcal{H}}\,\bigg\|Y\widehat\theta -\begin{pmatrix} \left<\Phi(x_1)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\\ \vdots\\ \left<\Phi(x_n)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, f\right>_{\mathcal{H}} \end{pmatrix}\bigg\|_{2}^{2}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Least-squares fit of the optimal scores by centered RKHS evaluations of $f$.

nodes.name: Representer Theorem
nodes.statement: By the Representer Theorem \cite{kimeldorf_correspondence_1970}, the minimizing $\widehat f$ lies in the finite-dimensional span of the centered data, that is it is sufficient to consider minimization over $f=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}[\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}]$ for some $\alpha_{i}\in \mathbb{R}$.
conclusions: the minimizing $\widehat f$ lies in the finite-dimensional span of the centered data
nodes.statement_short: The minimizer lies in the span of the centered feature maps of the data.

nodes.name: Coefficient-space kernel optimal scoring
nodes.statement: Combining the Representer Theorem with kernel representation of inner-products in $\mathcal{H}$ leads to the equivalent coefficient space formulation of the kernel optimal scoring problem: \begin{equation} \mathrm{minimize}_{\alpha\in \mathbb{R}^{n}}\,\|Y\widehat \theta-C\mathbf{K}C\alpha\|_{2}^{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: KOS as least squares in coefficients: minimize $\|Y\widehat\theta-CKC\alpha\|^2$ over $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Kernel optimal scoring problem (KOS)
nodes.statement: A common approach is to restrict the norm $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 = \alpha^{\top}CKC\alpha$, and we add a ridge penalty to the objective function~\eqref{eq:UnRegKernOptScore} \begin{equation} \mathrm{minimize}_{\alpha\in \mathbb{R}^n}\bigg\{\frac{1}{n}\|Y\widehat{\theta}-C\mathbf{K}C\alpha\|_{2}^{2}+\gamma \alpha^{\top}C\mathbf{K}C\alpha\bigg\}, \end{equation} where $\gamma > 0$ controls the level of regularization.
nodes.statement_short: Ridge-regularized kernel optimal scoring in coefficient space with penalty $\gamma\alpha^\top CKC\alpha$.

nodes.name: Numerical-stability ridge adjustment
nodes.statement: For numerical stability, we also add $\varepsilon I$ with small $\varepsilon > 0$ to the ridge penalty so that $CKC$ is replaced with $CKC + \varepsilon I$.

nodes.name: Closed-form KOS solution
nodes.statement: The problem has a closed-form solution leading to \begin{equation} \widehat{\alpha}= \{(C\mathbf{K}C)^2+n\gamma(C\mathbf{K}C+\varepsilon I)\}^{-1}C\mathbf{K}CY\widehat \theta. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: KOS coefficients $\widehat\alpha=\{(CKC)^2+n\gamma(CKC+\varepsilon I)\}^{-1}CKCY\widehat\theta$.

nodes.name: Kernel optimal scoring (KOS)
nodes.statement: We call~\eqref{eq:RegKernOptScore} the kernel optimal scoring problem or KOS.

nodes.name: Fitted discriminant function
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat \alpha$ be as in \eqref{eq:alpha}, and let $\widehat f = \sum_{i=1}^n \widehat \alpha_i[\Phi(x_i) - \overline \Phi]$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Classification of a New Data Point

nodes.name: Kernel evaluation vector
nodes.statement: Given a new data point $x\in \mathbb{R}^{p}$, let $$ K(X,x)= \begin{pmatrix} k(x_1, x)& \cdots& k(x_n,x)\end{pmatrix}^{\top}. $$
nodes.section: 2.4 Classification of a New Data Point

nodes.name: Projected value
nodes.statement: We define the projected value $P(x)$ as the inner-product between $x$ mapped and centered in $\mathcal{H}$ and $\widehat f$ so that $P(x)$ is equal to \begin{equation} \left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi},\, \widehat{f}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}=(K(X,x)^{\top}-n^{-1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{K})C\widehat\alpha. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.4 Classification of a New Data Point
nodes.statement_short: $P(x)$ is the RKHS inner product of the centered mapped point with $\widehat f$, computable from kernel evaluations.

nodes.name: KOS nearest-centroid classification rule
nodes.statement: KOS classifies $x\in \mathbb{R}^{p}$ using nearest centroids classification on the projected values. Specifically, let $\mu_k=\frac{1}{n_k}\sum_{i\in G_k}P(x_x)$ be the mean projected values of group $k$ (projected centroid). We classify $x\in \mathbb{R}^p$ according to the minimal distance to projected centroids $$ \mathrm{argmin}_{k=1,2} |P(x)-\mu_{k}|. $$
nodes.section: 2.4 Classification of a New Data Point
nodes.statement_short: Classify a new point to the class whose mean projected value is closest to $P(x)$.

nodes.name: Empirical risk
nodes.statement: Problem~\eqref{eq:RegKernOptScore} can be viewed as a regularized empirical risk minimization problem \begin{equation} \widehat f = \mathrm{argmin}_{f\in \mathcal{H}}\left\{R_{\text{emp}}(f) + \gamma \|f\|^2_{\mathcal{H}}\right\}, \end{equation} where for a fixed $f\in \mathcal{H}$ \begin{equation} R_{\text{emp}}(f):=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat{\theta}-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>|^{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: KOS is regularized empirical risk minimization with squared loss between scores and centered RKHS evaluations.

nodes.name: Constrained form of KOS
nodes.statement: By duality, for every $\gamma \geq 0$ there exists a $\tau \geq 0$ such that \begin{equation} \widehat f = \mathrm{argmin}_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq \tau}\left\{R_{\text{emp}}(f)\right\}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: By duality the penalized KOS solution equals a norm-constrained ERM solution for some radius $\tau$.
conclusions: there exists a $\tau \geq 0$ such that \begin{equation} \widehat f = \mathrm{argmin}_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq \tau}\left\{R_{\text{emp}}(f)\right\}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Bound on the constraint radius
nodes.statement: While the relationship between $\gamma$ and $\tau$ is data-dependent, Lemma~3 in the Supplement shows that $\tau \leq C\min(\gamma^{-1},\gamma^{-1/2})$ for some constant $C>0$.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring

nodes.name: Dependence of empirical-risk terms
nodes.statement: There are two complications in analyzing the empirical risk in~\eqref{eq:emprisk}: $\widehat{\theta}$ is dependent on all $y_i$ through $n_1$, $n_2$, and $\overline \Phi$ is dependent on all $x_i$. Hence, the error terms $|y_i^{\top}\widehat{\theta}-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>|^{2}$ are dependent.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat\theta$ and $\overline\Phi$ depend on the whole sample, so the empirical-risk terms are not independent.

nodes.name: Empirical risk with intercept
nodes.statement: The empirical risk can be equivalently written as $$ R_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat{\theta}-\beta -\left<\Phi(x_i),f\right>|^{2}, $$ with the minimizing $\widehat \beta =-\langle{\overline{\Phi}, f\rangle}$ since $\mathbf{1}^{\top}Y\widehat \theta = 0$.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: The empirical risk equals a squared loss with free intercept $\beta$, minimized at $\widehat\beta=-\langle\overline\Phi,f\rangle$.

nodes.name: Population scores
nodes.statement: Let $\pi_k = P(i\in C_k)$ be the prior class probabilities, $k=1,2$. The \emph{population scores} are defined as $\theta^*=( \sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}\ -\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2} )^{\top}$.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: Population scores replace sample proportions $n_k/n$ in $\widehat\theta$ by the priors $\pi_k$.
nodes.label: eq:PopulationScores

nodes.name: Modified empirical risk
nodes.statement: For a fixed $f\in\mathcal{H}$ and $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, the modified empirical risk is $$ \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x_i),f\right>|^{2}. $$
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring

nodes.name: Expected risk
nodes.statement: For a fixed $f\in \mathcal{H}$ and $\beta \in \mathbb{R}$, the corresponding expected risk is $$ R(f,\beta):=\mathbb{E}_{(x,y)}|y^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x),f\right>|^{2}. $$
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring

nodes.name: Fitted intercept
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat f$ be as in~\eqref{eq:constraint} and let $\widehat \beta = -\langle \overline{\Phi}, \widehat f\rangle$.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring

nodes.name: Non-degenerate class priors
nodes.statement: Let $\pi_{\max} = \max(\pi_1, \pi_2)$, $\pi_{\min} = \min(\pi_1, \pi_2)$. There exists a constant $C>0$ such that $\|\theta^*\|_\infty = \sqrt{\pi_{\max}/\pi_{\min}}\leq C$.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.label: assump:ScoreBound

nodes.name: Bounded kernel
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $\kappa>0$ such that $\|\Phi(x)\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq \kappa$ for all $x\in \mathbb{R}^{p}$. Equivalently, $ \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{p}} k(x,x)\leq \kappa^{2}.$
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring

nodes.name: Admissible functions and intercepts
nodes.statement: Using~\eqref{eq:constraint}, we define the set of admissible functions $f$ as $\mathcal{H}_{\tau}:=\{f\in\mathcal{H}: \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq \tau\}$, and the set of admissible intercepts $\beta$ as $I_{\tau}:=\{\beta \in \mathbb{R}: |\beta|\leq \|\theta^*\|_{\infty} + \kappa \tau\}$.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ is the RKHS ball of radius $\tau$; $I_\tau$ the interval of intercepts with $|\beta|\le\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau$.

nodes.name: Fitted intercept is admissible
nodes.statement: The intercept $\widehat \beta\in I_{\tau}$ by Assumption~\ref{assump:KernBound}. The extra term $\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}$ comes from minimizing the modified empirical risk.

nodes.name: Modified-empirical and expected risk minimizers
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} (\widetilde{f} , \widetilde{\beta}):=\mathrm{argmin}_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta). \end{equation} be the minimizers of the modified empirical risk over the set of admissible functions and intercepts, and let \begin{equation} (f^\ast, \beta^\ast)=\mathrm{argmin}_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau \,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} R(f, \beta) \end{equation} be the minimizers of the expected risk over the set of admissible functions and intercepts.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: $(\widetilde f,\widetilde\beta)$ minimize the modified empirical risk and $(f^*,\beta^*)$ the expected risk over admissible sets.

nodes.name: Excess expected risk bound for KOS
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions~\ref{assump:ScoreBound}--\ref{assump:Separable}, there exist constants $C_1, C_2, C_3>0$ such that \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)&>R(f^*,\beta^*)+\varepsilon \Big)\leq C_{1}\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(-\frac{C_3n \varepsilon^2}{(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)^4}\Big), \end{align*} where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\}\exp( C_2\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$.
nodes.section: 3 Error Bounds for Kernel Optimal Scoring
nodes.statement_short: With high probability the expected risk of the KOS estimator is within $\varepsilon$ of the best admissible expected risk.

nodes.name: Feature weight vector
nodes.statement: To incorporate feature selection, we borrow the ideas from \cite{allen_automatic_2013} and introduce a weight vector $w\in \mathbb{R}^p$, where we restrict each feature as $w_j \in [-1,1]$.

nodes.name: Weighted kernel matrix
nodes.statement: The weight vector is used to form the weighted kernel matrix $(\mathbf{K}_{w})_{i,j}=k(wx_i, wx_j)$, where $wx=(w_1 x_1, \dots, w_p x_p)^{\top}$ is the Hadamard product between the weight vector $w$ and observed feature vector $x$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbf{K}_w$ evaluates the kernel on feature vectors rescaled coordinatewise by $w$.

nodes.name: Sparse kernel optimal scoring problem
nodes.statement: We adjust~\eqref{eq:RegKernOptScore} to perform joint minimization over the coefficient vector $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and the weight vector $w\in \mathbb{R}^p$. To encourage feature selection, we add an $\ell_1$-penalty on $w$ as in \cite{allen_automatic_2013} leading to the following minimization problem: \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathrm{minimize}_{\alpha\in \mathbb{R}^{n},\,w\in \mathbb{R}^{p}}\bigg\{ \frac{1}{n}&\|Y\widehat{\theta}-C\mathbf{K}_wC\alpha\|_{2}^{2}+\lambda\|w\|_{1}+\gamma \alpha^{\top}(C\mathbf{K}_wC+\varepsilon I)\alpha\bigg\}\\ \text{subject to}&\quad-1\leq w_i\leq 1\text{ for }i=1, \dots, p. \end{split} \end{equation} Here $\lambda \geq 0$ is the tuning parameter that controls the sparsity of the weight vector $w$, with larger values leading to sparser solutions.
nodes.statement_short: Joint minimization over $\alpha$ and box-constrained weights $w$ of the KOS objective with weighted kernel plus $\lambda\|w\|_1$.

nodes.name: Sparse kernel optimal scoring
nodes.statement: We call~\eqref{eq:ObjFun} sparse kernel optimal scoring.

nodes.name: Sparse KOS classification rule
nodes.statement: Given the solution pair $(\widehat w, \widehat \alpha)$, we perform classification as in Section~\ref{sec:Projection} with $\mathbf{K}_{\widehat w}$ being substituted for $\mathbf{K}$ and $\widehat w x$ substituted for $x$ in forming the projected values $P(x)$ in~\eqref{eq:Projection}.

nodes.name: Sign of the weights
nodes.statement: Unlike our restriction $w_k\in [-1,1]$, \cite{allen_automatic_2013} considers $w_k \in [0,1]$. Both lead to $w_k^2\in [0,1]$, but we found that the latter may force all the weights to zero even when $\lambda = 0$. This behavior is avoided when the weights are allowed to be negative.

nodes.name: Sparse KOS objective function
nodes.statement: We define the objective function in~\eqref{eq:ObjFun} as \begin{equation} \begin{split} Obj(w, \alpha)& = \frac{1}{n}\|Y\widehat{\theta}-C\mathbf{K}_wC\alpha\|_{2}^{2}+\lambda\|w\|_{1}+\gamma \alpha^{\top}(C\mathbf{K}_wC+\varepsilon I)\alpha. \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Linearized weighted kernel
nodes.statement: Consider the first-order Taylor approximation of $\mathbf{K}_{w}$ with respect to $w$ centered at the previous value $w^{(t-1)}$ elementwise: \begin{align*} \widetilde{\mathbf{K}}_{w}(x_i,x_j):=\mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}(x_i, x_j)+\{\nabla_{w}\mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}(x_i, x_j)\}^{\top}(w-w^{(t-1)}), \end{align*} where $\nabla_w\mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}(x_i, x_j)\in \mathbb{R}^p$ is the gradient of $k(wx_i, wx_j)$ with respect to $w$ evaluated at $w^{(t-1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: First-order Taylor expansion of each weighted-kernel entry in $w$ around the previous iterate.

nodes.name: Gradient matrix T
nodes.statement: Let $T\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$ be $$ T := \begin{pmatrix} \sum_{\ell=1}^{n}(C\alpha)_{\ell}\nabla_{w}\, \mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}(x_1, x_\ell)^{\top}\\ \vdots\\ \sum_{\ell=1}^{n}(C\alpha)_{\ell}\nabla_{w}\, \mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}(x_n, x_\ell)^{\top} \end{pmatrix}. $$

nodes.name: Weighted-lasso subproblem in w
nodes.statement: For fixed $\alpha$, the minimization problem~\eqref{eq:ObjFun} with respect to $w$ can be written as \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\mathrm{minimize}_{w} \bigg\{\frac{1}{2}w^{\top}Qw-\beta^{\top}w+ \frac{\lambda}{2}\|w\|_{1}\bigg\}\\ &\text{subject to }-1\leq w_i\leq 1\text{ for }i=1, \dots, p; \end{split} \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \begin{split} &Q=\frac{1}{n}(CT)^{\top}CT \in \mathbb{R}^{p\times p},\\ &\beta=\frac{1}{n}T^{\top}C [Y\widehat{\theta}-C\mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}C\alpha+CTw^{(t-1)}]-2^{-1}\gamma T^{\top}C\alpha\in \mathbb{R}^{p}. \end{split} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For fixed $\alpha$ the linearized $w$-update is a box-constrained lasso-type quadratic program with $Q$ and $\beta$ built from $T$.

nodes.name: Sparse Kernel Optimal Scoring algorithm
nodes.statement: \SetAlgoLined \caption{Sparse Kernel Optimal Scoring} \SetKwInOut{Input}{Input} \SetKwInOut{Output}{Output} \DontPrintSemicolon \Input{$X\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$, $Y\in \mathbb{R}^{n \times 2}$, $\widehat \theta$, $\sigma >0$, $\gamma >0$, $\lambda \geq 0$ , convergence threshold $\varepsilon_{\text{con}}$} \Output{Discriminant coefficients $\widehat{\alpha}$ and feature weights $\widehat{w}$.} $t\gets 0$\; $w^{(0)} \gets \mathbf{1}$\; $(\mathbf{K}_{w^{(0)}})_{i,j} \gets k(w^0 x_i, w^0 x_j)$, $\mathbf{K}_{w^{(0)}}\gets \{(\mathbf{K}_{w_0})_{i,j}\}$\; \Repeat{$\mbox{\textrm{Obj}}(\alpha^{(t)}, w^{(t)})-\mbox{Obj}(\alpha^{(t-1)}, w^{(t-1)})< \varepsilon_{\text{con}}$}{ $t\gets t+1$\; Update $\alpha^{(t)}$ according to~\eqref{eq:alpha} with $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}$\; Update $w^{(t)}$ using coordinate descent with updates according to~\eqref{eq:wupdate}\; $(\mathbf{K}_{w^{(t)}})_{i,j}\gets k(w^{(t)}x_i, w^{(t)}x_j)$\; } \Return{$\widehat{\alpha}=\alpha^{(t)}$, $\widehat{w}=w^{(t)}$}
nodes.statement_short: Alternating minimization: closed-form ridge update of $\alpha$, then coordinate-descent update of the linearized weights $w$, until the objective stalls.
nodes.label: a:algorithm

nodes.name: Set iteration counter
nodes.statement: \SetAlgoLined \caption{Sparse Kernel Optimal Scoring} \SetKwInOut{Input}{Input} \SetKwInOut{Output}{Output} \DontPrintSemicolon \Input{$X\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$, $Y\in \mathbb{R}^{n \times 2}$, $\widehat \theta$, $\sigma >0$, $\gamma >0$, $\lambda \geq 0$ , convergence threshold $\varepsilon_{\text{con}}$} \Output{Discriminant coefficients $\widehat{\alpha}$ and feature weights $\widehat{w}$.} $t\gets 0$
nodes.statement_short: Declare inputs/outputs and set $t=0$.

nodes.name: Initialize weights to ones
nodes.statement: $w^{(0)} \gets \mathbf{1}$

nodes.name: Initial kernel matrix
nodes.statement: $(\mathbf{K}_{w^{(0)}})_{i,j} \gets k(w^0 x_i, w^0 x_j)$, $\mathbf{K}_{w^{(0)}}\gets \{(\mathbf{K}_{w_0})_{i,j}\}$
nodes.statement_short: Form the initial (unweighted) kernel matrix.

nodes.name: Repeat until objective converges
nodes.statement: \Repeat{$\mbox{\textrm{Obj}}(\alpha^{(t)}, w^{(t)})-\mbox{Obj}(\alpha^{(t-1)}, w^{(t-1)})< \varepsilon_{\text{con}}$}{ $t\gets t+1$\; Update $\alpha^{(t)}$ according to~\eqref{eq:alpha} with $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}$\; Update $w^{(t)}$ using coordinate descent with updates according to~\eqref{eq:wupdate}\; $(\mathbf{K}_{w^{(t)}})_{i,j}\gets k(w^{(t)}x_i, w^{(t)}x_j)$

nodes.name: Increment counter
nodes.statement: $t\gets t+1$

nodes.name: Ridge update of alpha
nodes.statement: Update $\alpha^{(t)}$ according to~\eqref{eq:alpha} with $\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{K}_{w^{(t-1)}}$
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form KOS update of $\alpha$ with the current weighted kernel.

nodes.name: Coordinate-descent update of w
nodes.statement: Update $w^{(t)}$ using coordinate descent with updates according to~\eqref{eq:wupdate}
nodes.statement_short: Solve the linearized weighted-lasso problem for $w$ by coordinate descent.

nodes.name: Recompute weighted kernel
nodes.statement: $(\mathbf{K}_{w^{(t)}})_{i,j}\gets k(w^{(t)}x_i, w^{(t)}x_j)$
nodes.statement_short: Recompute the weighted kernel with the new weights.

nodes.name: Convergence test
nodes.statement: $\mbox{\textrm{Obj}}(\alpha^{(t)}, w^{(t)})-\mbox{Obj}(\alpha^{(t-1)}, w^{(t-1)})< \varepsilon_{\text{con}}$
nodes.statement_short: Stop when the objective decrease falls below the threshold.

nodes.name: Return estimates
nodes.statement: \Return{$\widehat{\alpha}=\alpha^{(t)}$, $\widehat{w}=w^{(t)}$}

nodes.name: Lasso form of the w-subproblem
nodes.statement: Problem~\eqref{eq:wlasso} is of the same form as the penalized lasso problem \cite[Chapter 5]{hastie2015statistical} with extra convex constraints on $w$. Therefore, we can use the coordinate-descent algorithm to solve~\eqref{eq:wlasso}.

nodes.name: Coordinate-descent update for w
nodes.statement: Consider optimizing~\eqref{eq:wlasso} with respect to $w_k$. From the KKT conditions~\cite{boyd2004convex}, the solution must satisfy \begin{equation} \widehat w_k = \mathrm{sign}(\widetilde w_k)\min(|\widetilde w_k|, 1), \end{equation} where $$ \widetilde{w}_{k}:=\frac{1}{Q_{kk}}S_{\lambda/2}\bigg(\beta_k-\sum_{i\neq k}Q_{ki}w_{i} \bigg), $$ and $S_{\lambda/2}(x):=\text{sign}(x) \max\{|x|-\lambda/2,\, 0\}$ is the soft-thresholding function.
nodes.statement_short: KKT conditions give the coordinate update: soft-threshold the partial residual, rescale by $Q_{kk}$, and clip to $[-1,1]$.

nodes.name: Coordinate-descent algorithm for the w-subproblem
nodes.statement: The coordinate-descent algorithm proceeds by applying the update~\eqref{eq:wupdate} on each feature $k$ until convergence.
nodes.statement_short: Cycle the clipped soft-thresholding update over coordinates of $w$ until convergence.

nodes.name: Empirical monotone decrease of the objective
nodes.statement: While the update of $w$ is based on approximation of objective function~\eqref{eq:ObjectiveFunction}, in our experience the objective function is always decreasing at each iteration.

nodes.name: Gaussian kernel parameter selection
nodes.statement: We propose to use 5-fold cross-validation to minimize the error rate. To reduce computational cost, we only consider five tuning parameters based on the $\{.05, .1, .2, .3,.5\}$ quantiles of the set of squared distances between the classes $$ \{\|x_{i_1}-x_{i_2}\|_2^2\,:x_{i_1} \in C_1,\,x_{i_2}\in C_2\}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\sigma^2$ by 5-fold CV among five lower quantiles of between-class squared distances.

nodes.name: Noise features inflate distances
nodes.statement: We find that this yields good predictive accuracy, and we conjecture that the reason is the presence of noise features, which inflate the distance values $\|x_{i_1}-x_{i_2}\|_2$. This is supported by empirical observation that the quantiles based on the full set of features will exceed the corresponding quantiles based on the reduced set of informative features.

nodes.name: Stabilization
nodes.statement: Following~\cite{lancewicki_regularization_2017}, in KOS we want to stabilize $(C\mathbf{K}_wC)^{2}$ with the target matrix $C\mathbf{K}_w C+\varepsilon I$, and therefore consider $$ (C\mathbf{K}_wC)^{2} + \gamma (C\mathbf{K}_w C+\varepsilon I) $$ for $\gamma >0$. Let $t = \gamma/(1+\gamma)$, then the optimal value of $t$ is $\widehat t = \min(\max(0, \widetilde t), 1)$, where $$\widetilde{t}:=\frac{n}{(n-2)}\bigg(\frac{\|\text{diag}(C\mathbf{K}C)\|_{F}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\|C\mathbf{K}C\|_{F}^{2}}{\|C\mathbf{K}C\|_{F}^{2}}\bigg).$$ Solving back for $\gamma$ gives the ridge penalty $\widehat{\gamma}=\widehat{t}/(1-\widehat{t})$. We call this approach Stabilization.
nodes.statement_short: Choose the ridge parameter by optimal shrinkage of $(CK_wC)^2$ toward $CK_wC+\varepsilon I$, then convert the shrinkage weight to $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Sparsity parameter selection
nodes.statement: We select $\lambda$ using 5-fold cross-validation (CV) to minimize the error rate over a grid of 20 equally-spaced values in $[10^{-10}\lambda_{\text{max}}, \lambda_\text{max}]$. We set $\lambda_{\max} = 2 \|\beta\|_\infty$, where $\beta$ is as in~\eqref{eq:QandB}, since the solution $\widehat w$ to~\eqref{eq:wlasso} is zero if $\lambda \geq \lambda_{\max}$ (see Lemma~1 in the Supplement).
nodes.statement_short: Pick $\lambda$ by 5-fold CV over 20 grid values up to $\lambda_{\max}=2\|\beta\|_\infty$, above which $\widehat w=0$.

nodes.name: Cross-validate the kernel parameter
nodes.statement: We propose to use 5-fold cross-validation to minimize the error rate.
nodes.statement_short: Select the kernel parameter by 5-fold CV.

nodes.name: Candidate grid from distance quantiles
nodes.statement: To reduce computational cost, we only consider five tuning parameters based on the $\{.05, .1, .2, .3,.5\}$ quantiles of the set of squared distances between the classes $$ \{\|x_{i_1}-x_{i_2}\|_2^2\,:x_{i_1} \in C_1,\,x_{i_2}\in C_2\}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Candidates are five lower quantiles of between-class squared distances.

nodes.name: Shrinkage form of the ridge-regularized matrix
nodes.statement: Following~\cite{lancewicki_regularization_2017}, in KOS we want to stabilize $(C\mathbf{K}_wC)^{2}$ with the target matrix $C\mathbf{K}_w C+\varepsilon I$, and therefore consider $$ (C\mathbf{K}_wC)^{2} + \gamma (C\mathbf{K}_w C+\varepsilon I) $$ for $\gamma >0$.
nodes.statement_short: Regard the ridge penalty as shrinkage of $(CK_wC)^2$ toward $CK_wC+\varepsilon I$.

nodes.name: Optimal shrinkage intensity
nodes.statement: Let $t = \gamma/(1+\gamma)$, then the optimal value of $t$ is $\widehat t = \min(\max(0, \widetilde t), 1)$, where $$\widetilde{t}:=\frac{n}{(n-2)}\bigg(\frac{\|\text{diag}(C\mathbf{K}C)\|_{F}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\|C\mathbf{K}C\|_{F}^{2}}{\|C\mathbf{K}C\|_{F}^{2}}\bigg).$$
nodes.statement_short: Compute the clipped optimal shrinkage intensity $\widehat t$.

nodes.name: Convert to ridge parameter
nodes.statement: Solving back for $\gamma$ gives the ridge penalty $\widehat{\gamma}=\widehat{t}/(1-\widehat{t})$.

nodes.name: Cross-validate lambda over a grid
nodes.statement: We select $\lambda$ using 5-fold cross-validation (CV) to minimize the error rate over a grid of 20 equally-spaced values in $[10^{-10}\lambda_{\text{max}}, \lambda_\text{max}]$.

nodes.name: Set the grid maximum
nodes.statement: We set $\lambda_{\max} = 2 \|\beta\|_\infty$, where $\beta$ is as in~\eqref{eq:QandB}, since the solution $\widehat w$ to~\eqref{eq:wlasso} is zero if $\lambda \geq \lambda_{\max}$ (see Lemma~1 in the Supplement).
nodes.statement_short: Set $\lambda_{\max}=2\|\beta\|_\infty$, the smallest value giving $\widehat w=0$.

nodes.name: Derivation of the projection formula
nodes.statement: Since $\widehat f = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \widehat \alpha_{i}[\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}]$, \begin{align*} \left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}&=\left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, \sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat \alpha_{i}[\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}]\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}, \Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i\left<\Phi(x), \Phi(x_i)\right>_{\mathcal{H}}- \sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\Phi(x), \overline{\Phi}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}- \sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\overline{\Phi}, \Phi(x_i)\right>_{\mathcal{H}}+ \sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\overline{\Phi}, \overline{\Phi}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_ik(x, x_i) - (\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha)\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^nk(x, x_i) - \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i k(x_j, x_i) + (\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha) \frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n k(x_i, x_j). \end{align*} Let $K(X,x):=\begin{pmatrix} k(x_1, x)&\cdots&k(x_n, x) \end{pmatrix}^{\top}$. Then from the above display \begin{align*} \left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}} &=K(X,x)^{\top}\widehat \alpha - n^{-1}K(X,x)^{\top}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha - n^{-1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\widehat \alpha + \frac1{n^2}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}(\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha)\\ &=K(X,x)^{\top}C\widehat \alpha - \frac1{n}\mathbf{1}^{\top}KC\widehat \alpha\\ &= (K(X,x)^{\top} - \frac1{n}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K)C\widehat \alpha, \end{align*} where $C = I - n^{-1}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}$ is the centering matrix.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the RKHS inner product of the centered point with $\widehat f$ by bilinearity and rewrite kernel sums in matrix form.

nodes.name: Expand the inner product into kernel sums by bilinearity
nodes.statement: Since $\widehat f = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \widehat \alpha_{i}[\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}]$, \begin{align*} \left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}&=\left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, \sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat \alpha_{i}[\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}]\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}, \Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i\left<\Phi(x), \Phi(x_i)\right>_{\mathcal{H}}- \sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\Phi(x), \overline{\Phi}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}- \sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\overline{\Phi}, \Phi(x_i)\right>_{\mathcal{H}}+ \sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i \left<\overline{\Phi}, \overline{\Phi}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat \alpha_ik(x, x_i) - (\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha)\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^nk(x, x_i) - \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n\widehat \alpha_i k(x_j, x_i) + (\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha) \frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n k(x_i, x_j). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the inner product into kernel sums by bilinearity

nodes.name: Write the sums in matrix form with the centering matrix
nodes.statement: Let $K(X,x):=\begin{pmatrix} k(x_1, x)&\cdots&k(x_n, x) \end{pmatrix}^{\top}$. Then from the above display \begin{align*} \left<\Phi(x)-\overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}} &=K(X,x)^{\top}\widehat \alpha - n^{-1}K(X,x)^{\top}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha - n^{-1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\widehat \alpha + \frac1{n^2}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K\mathbf{1}(\mathbf{1}^{\top}\widehat \alpha)\\ &=K(X,x)^{\top}C\widehat \alpha - \frac1{n}\mathbf{1}^{\top}KC\widehat \alpha\\ &= (K(X,x)^{\top} - \frac1{n}\mathbf{1}^{\top}K)C\widehat \alpha, \end{align*} where $C = I - n^{-1}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}$ is the centering matrix.
