nodes.name: Constant convention
nodes.statement: We use $C$, $C_1$, $C_2$, $\dots$ to denote absolute positive constants that do not depend on the sample size $n$ but which may depend on $\|\theta^*\|_\infty, \kappa,$ or $\tau$. Their values may change from line to line.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Consider \begin{align*} R(\widehat{f},\widehat{\beta})- R(f^\ast,\beta^\ast)=\underbrace{R(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})}_{I_1}+\underbrace{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})}_{I_2} +\underbrace{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})- R(f^\ast,\beta^\ast)}_{I_3}. \end{align*} By the union bound and de Morgan's law, \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R(f^*,\beta^*)>\varepsilon\Big)\,\leq \,\mathbb{P}\Big( I_1 >\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big( I_2 >\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+ \mathbb{P}\Big( I_3 >\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big). \end{align*} Applying Theorems~\ref{thm:SymBound},~\ref{thm:ModRiskDiffConverge} and~\ref{thm:ModConsistency} to $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ correspondingly, there exist constants $C,C_i >0$ such that \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(R(\widehat{f},\widehat{\beta})&- R(f^\ast,\beta^\ast)>\varepsilon\Big)\\ &\leq 2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big)+C_2\exp\Big( -\frac{C_3n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big)+2\exp\Big(-\frac{n \varepsilon^2}{16(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^4}\Big)\\ &\leq C_4\, \mathcal{N_\varepsilon}\exp\Big(-\frac{C_5 n \varepsilon^2}{(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^4}\Big), \end{align*} where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp( C\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$. This concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:EstErrorProbBound}.
nodes.statement_short: Split the excess risk into three terms, union bound, and bound each by Theorems 3, 4 and 5.

nodes.name: Decompose excess risk into $I_1+I_2+I_3$
nodes.statement: Consider \begin{align*} R(\widehat{f},\widehat{\beta})- R(f^\ast,\beta^\ast)=\underbrace{R(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})}_{I_1}+\underbrace{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})}_{I_2} +\underbrace{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})- R(f^\ast,\beta^\ast)}_{I_3}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose excess risk into $I_1+I_2+I_3$

nodes.name: Union bound over the three terms
nodes.statement: By the union bound and de Morgan's law, \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R(f^*,\beta^*)>\varepsilon\Big)\,\leq \,\mathbb{P}\Big( I_1 >\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big( I_2 >\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+ \mathbb{P}\Big( I_3 >\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over the three terms

nodes.name: Apply Theorems 3-5 to each term and combine
nodes.statement: Applying Theorems~\ref{thm:SymBound},~\ref{thm:ModRiskDiffConverge} and~\ref{thm:ModConsistency} to $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ correspondingly, there exist constants $C,C_i >0$ such that \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(R(\widehat{f},\widehat{\beta})&- R(f^\ast,\beta^\ast)>\varepsilon\Big)\\ &\leq 2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big)+C_2\exp\Big( -\frac{C_3n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big)+2\exp\Big(-\frac{n \varepsilon^2}{16(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^4}\Big)\\ &\leq C_4\, \mathcal{N_\varepsilon}\exp\Big(-\frac{C_5 n \varepsilon^2}{(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^4}\Big), \end{align*} where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp( C\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$. This concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:EstErrorProbBound}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorems 3-5 to each term and combine

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Consider \begin{align*} R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)&= \underbrace{R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)}_{I_1}+\underbrace{\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)}_{I_2}. \end{align*} By the union bound and de Morgan's law, $$ \mathbb{P}\Big( R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\Big(I_{1}>\frac{\varepsilon}{2} \Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big( I_2 >\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\Big). $$ Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:SymBound} for $I_1$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:DifferenceRiskSupConverge} for $I_2$, the exist constants $C_i > 0$ such that \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big( R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)>\varepsilon\Big)&\leq 2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big)+ C_3 \exp\Big( -\frac{C_4n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big)\\ &\leq C_5 \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(-\frac{C_6 n \varepsilon^2}{(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big), \end{align*} where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp(C_1\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$. This concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:EmpRiskProbBound}.
nodes.statement_short: Split the gap into two terms, union bound, and bound them by Theorems 3 and 6.

nodes.name: Decompose the gap into $I_1+I_2$
nodes.statement: Consider \begin{align*} R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)&= \underbrace{R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)}_{I_1}+\underbrace{\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)}_{I_2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the gap into $I_1+I_2$

nodes.name: Union bound over the two terms
nodes.statement: By the union bound and de Morgan's law, $$ \mathbb{P}\Big( R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\Big(I_{1}>\frac{\varepsilon}{2} \Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big( I_2 >\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\Big). $$
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over the two terms

nodes.name: Apply Theorems 3 and 6 and combine
nodes.statement: Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:SymBound} for $I_1$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:DifferenceRiskSupConverge} for $I_2$, the exist constants $C_i > 0$ such that \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big( R(\widehat f, \widehat \beta)-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)>\varepsilon\Big)&\leq 2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big)+ C_3 \exp\Big( -\frac{C_4n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big)\\ &\leq C_5 \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(-\frac{C_6 n \varepsilon^2}{(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big), \end{align*} where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp(C_1\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$. This concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:EmpRiskProbBound}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorems 3 and 6 and combine

nodes.name: Uniform deviation bound via symmetrization
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assump:ScoreBound}-\ref{assump:Separable}, there exists a constant $C_2 > 0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$, $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau}\{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta)\}>\varepsilon\Big) \leq 2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big), $$ where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp( C_2\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform deviation of expected over modified empirical risk on the admissible class is exponentially small, with covering factor $\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon$.
conclusions: there exists a constant $C_2 > 0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$, $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau}\{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta)\}>\varepsilon\Big) \leq 2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big), $$ where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp( C_2\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$.
nodes.label: thm:SymBound

nodes.name: Modified risk of KOS estimator vs modified-risk minimizer
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat{\beta}=-\left<\,\overline{\Phi}, \widehat{f}\,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}$. Under Assumptions \ref{assump:ScoreBound} and \ref{assump:KernBound}, there exist constants $C_1, C_2>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0,$ \[ \mathbb{P}\Big(\Big| \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\Big|>\varepsilon\Big) \leq C_1\exp\Big( -\frac{C_2n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: The modified empirical risk of the KOS fit is close to that of the modified-risk minimizer with high probability.
conclusions: there exist constants $C_1, C_2>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0,$ \[ \mathbb{P}\Big(\Big| \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\Big|>\varepsilon\Big) \leq C_1\exp\Big( -\frac{C_2n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big). \]
nodes.label: thm:ModRiskDiffConverge

nodes.name: Consistency of modified empirical risk minimizer
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assump:ScoreBound} and \ref{assump:KernBound}, for all $\varepsilon>0$ $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde f, \widetilde \beta)-R(f^\ast, \beta^\ast) >\varepsilon \Big) \leq 2\exp\Big( -\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{16(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)^{4}}\Big). $$
nodes.statement_short: The modified empirical risk minimum exceeds the best expected risk by more than $\varepsilon$ with exponentially small probability.
nodes.label: thm:ModConsistency

nodes.name: Uniform closeness of empirical and modified empirical risk
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{assump:ScoreBound} and \ref{assump:KernBound} be true, and let $\beta(f):=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^ny_i^{\top}\theta^*-\left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}= \overline{Y\theta^*} - \left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}$ be the minimizing $\beta\in I_\tau$ for fixed $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}$ in the modified empirical risk. There exists constants $C_1,C_2>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$ \[ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau} |R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))|>\varepsilon \Big)\leq C_1 \exp\Big( -\frac{C_2n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Uniformly over $\mathcal{H}_\tau$, empirical risk and modified empirical risk with optimal intercept are close w.h.p.
assumptions: $\beta(f):=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^ny_i^{\top}\theta^*-\left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}= \overline{Y\theta^*} - \left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}$ be the minimizing $\beta\in I_\tau$ for fixed $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}$ in the modified empirical risk
conclusions: There exists constants $C_1,C_2>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$ \[ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau} |R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))|>\varepsilon \Big)\leq C_1 \exp\Big( -\frac{C_2n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big). \]
nodes.label: thm:DifferenceRiskSupConverge

nodes.name: Empirical measure and L2(T_x) semi-norm
nodes.statement: The \emph{empirical measure} $T_x$ with respect to $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{n}$ is defined as $T_{x}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \delta(x_i),$ where $\delta(x_i)$ is the point mass at $x_i$. The space $L^{2}(T_{x})$ is the set $\mathcal{H}_{\tau}$ equipped with the semi-norm \[ \|f \|_{L^2(T_{x})}:=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} |f(x_i)|^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\left<\Phi(x_i),f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: $T_x$ puts mass $1/n$ on each sample point; $L^2(T_x)$ is $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ with the empirical root-mean-square semi-norm.

nodes.name: Epsilon-net and covering number
nodes.statement: Let $(X,d)$ be a pseudometric space. An $\varepsilon$-net is any subset $\widetilde{X}\subset X$ such that for any $x\in X$, there exists a $\widetilde{x}\in \widetilde{X}$ satisfying $d(x,\widetilde{x})<\varepsilon$. The $\varepsilon$-\emph{covering number} of $(X,d)$ is the minimum size of an $\varepsilon$-net for $X$.
differentia: for any $x\in X$, there exists a $\widetilde{x}\in \widetilde{X}$ satisfying $d(x,\widetilde{x})<\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Distances on admissible sets
nodes.statement: Distances in $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ are given by the semi-norm generated by $L^2(T_x)$. Distances in $I_\tau$ are given by the Euclidean distance $d(\beta_1, \beta_2)=|\beta_1-\beta_2|.$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Let $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{j=n+1}^{2n}$ be independent from $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$ and identically distributed set of $n$ pairs, and let $T_x$ be the empirical measure on $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{2n}$. Let $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ be the modified empirical risk on $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$, and $\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ on $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{i=n+1}^{2n}$. By symmetrization lemma (see, for example, Lemma 2 in \cite{bousquet2004introduction}), for $n\varepsilon^2\geq 2$ \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\varepsilon\bigg)\leq 2\mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\bigg). \end{align*} Let $c = 64(\|\theta^*\|_{\infty} + \kappa \tau)$, and let $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ be the smallest $L^2(T_x)$ $\varepsilon/\sqrt{2}c$-net of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ and $\{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ an $\varepsilon/c$-net of $I_\tau$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:EpsilonNetInSymmetrization} to the above display \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\varepsilon\bigg)&\leq 2\mathbb{P}\bigg(\mathrm{maximize}_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}}\{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\bigg). \end{align*} Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:MaxBound} to the right-hand expression gives the final inequality \begin{align*} &\mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\varepsilon\bigg)\\ &\qquad\qquad\leq 2\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp\Big( \frac{C_1\tau^2}{\varepsilon^2}\Big) \exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big). \end{align*} This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:SymBound}.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrization with a ghost sample, discretize by $\varepsilon$-nets (Lemma 4), then union bound plus Hoeffding over the nets (Lemma 5).

nodes.name: Introduce ghost sample and its risks
nodes.statement: Let $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{j=n+1}^{2n}$ be independent from $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$ and identically distributed set of $n$ pairs, and let $T_x$ be the empirical measure on $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{2n}$. Let $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ be the modified empirical risk on $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$, and $\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ on $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{i=n+1}^{2n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce ghost sample and its risks

nodes.name: Apply the symmetrization lemma
nodes.statement: By symmetrization lemma (see, for example, Lemma 2 in \cite{bousquet2004introduction}), for $n\varepsilon^2\geq 2$ \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\varepsilon\bigg)\leq 2\mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\bigg). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the symmetrization lemma

nodes.name: Restrict to $\varepsilon$-nets via Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Let $c = 64(\|\theta^*\|_{\infty} + \kappa \tau)$, and let $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ be the smallest $L^2(T_x)$ $\varepsilon/\sqrt{2}c$-net of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ and $\{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ an $\varepsilon/c$-net of $I_\tau$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:EpsilonNetInSymmetrization} to the above display \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\varepsilon\bigg)&\leq 2\mathbb{P}\bigg(\mathrm{maximize}_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}}\{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\bigg). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to $\varepsilon$-nets via Lemma 4

nodes.name: Bound the maximum over the nets by Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:MaxBound} to the right-hand expression gives the final inequality \begin{align*} &\mathbb{P}\bigg( \sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau\,,\, \beta\in I_\tau} \{R(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_\text{emp}(f,\beta)\}>\varepsilon\bigg)\\ &\qquad\qquad\leq 2\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp\Big( \frac{C_1\tau^2}{\varepsilon^2}\Big) \exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big). \end{align*} This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:SymBound}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the maximum over the nets by Lemma 5

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement: Let $\beta(f) = \overline{Y\theta^*}-\left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}$. By definition of $\widetilde f$, $\widetilde \beta = \beta(\widetilde f)$, $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta}) \geq \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde {f}, \widetilde{\beta})$. On the other hand, since $R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)\leq R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde f)$, \begin{align*} \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})&= \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f})+R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f})-R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})+ R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\\ &\leq \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}) + R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\\ &\leq \widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \widehat \beta) - \widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \beta(\widehat f)) + \widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \beta(\widehat f)) -R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f})+ R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\\ &\leq \underbrace{\Big|\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \beta(\widehat f))\Big|}_{I_1} +2\underbrace{\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau} \Big| R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))\Big|}_{I_2}. \end{align*} The union bound and de Morgan's law proves $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\Big( I_1>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big( I_2>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\Big). $$ Consider $I_1$ \begin{align*} &\Big|\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \beta(\widehat f))\Big|\\ &= \Big| \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big(y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big)^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big(y_i^{\top}\theta^* - \overline{Y\theta^*}-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, \widehat{f}\,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big)^{2} \Big|\\ &=\Big|2\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\overline{Y\theta^*}\Big(y_i^{\top}\theta^* - \left<\Phi(x_i) - \overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big) - \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n(\overline{Y\theta^*})^2\Big|\\ &=\Big|(\overline{Y\theta^*})^2 - 2(\overline{Y\theta^*})\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\left<\Phi(x_i) - \overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big|\\ &= |\overline{Y\theta^*}|^2. \end{align*} By Lemma~\ref{lem:ytheta}, there exists $C_1>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(I_1>\varepsilon/2)\leq 2\exp(-C_1 n \varepsilon)$ for all $\varepsilon>0.$ By Theorem~\ref{thm:DifferenceRiskSupConverge}, there exists constants $C_2, C_3>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(I_2>\varepsilon/2)\leq C_2 \exp[-C_3 (n \varepsilon^2)/\{1+(\kappa\tau)^2\}].$ Combining the bounds for $I_1$ and $I_2$ gives \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})>\varepsilon\Big) &\leq 2\exp(-C_1 n \varepsilon)+C_2 \exp\Big(-\frac{C_3 n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big)\\ &\leq C_4\exp\Big(-\frac{C_5 n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big) \end{align*} for some constants $C_i>0$. This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:ModRiskDiffConverge}.
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich the risk difference using optimality of $\widehat f$ and $\widetilde f$, then bound the intercept term by Lemma 7 and the uniform term by Theorem 6.

nodes.name: Lower bound from optimality of $\widetilde f$
nodes.statement: Let $\beta(f) = \overline{Y\theta^*}-\left<\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}$. By definition of $\widetilde f$, $\widetilde \beta = \beta(\widetilde f)$, $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta}) \geq \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde {f}, \widetilde{\beta})$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound from optimality of $\widetilde f$

nodes.name: Upper bound by intercept term and uniform term
nodes.statement: On the other hand, since $R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f)\leq R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde f)$, \begin{align*} \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})&= \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f})+R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f})-R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})+ R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\\ &\leq \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}) + R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\\ &\leq \widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \widehat \beta) - \widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \beta(\widehat f)) + \widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat f, \beta(\widehat f)) -R_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f})+ R_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\\ &\leq \underbrace{\Big|\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \beta(\widehat f))\Big|}_{I_1} +2\underbrace{\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau} \Big| R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))\Big|}_{I_2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound by intercept term and uniform term

nodes.name: Union bound over $I_1$, $I_2$
nodes.statement: The union bound and de Morgan's law proves $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\Big( I_1>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big( I_2>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\Big). $$
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over $I_1$, $I_2$

nodes.name: Compute $I_1=|\overline{Y\theta^*}|^2$
nodes.statement: Consider $I_1$ \begin{align*} &\Big|\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \beta(\widehat f))\Big|\\ &= \Big| \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big(y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big)^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big(y_i^{\top}\theta^* - \overline{Y\theta^*}-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\,,\, \widehat{f}\,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big)^{2} \Big|\\ &=\Big|2\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\overline{Y\theta^*}\Big(y_i^{\top}\theta^* - \left<\Phi(x_i) - \overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big) - \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n(\overline{Y\theta^*})^2\Big|\\ &=\Big|(\overline{Y\theta^*})^2 - 2(\overline{Y\theta^*})\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\left<\Phi(x_i) - \overline{\Phi}, \widehat f \,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big|\\ &= |\overline{Y\theta^*}|^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute $I_1=|\overline{Y\theta^*}|^2$

nodes.name: Bound $I_1$ by Lemma 7
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:ytheta}, there exists $C_1>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(I_1>\varepsilon/2)\leq 2\exp(-C_1 n \varepsilon)$ for all $\varepsilon>0.$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $I_1$ by Lemma 7

nodes.name: Bound $I_2$ by Theorem 6
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{thm:DifferenceRiskSupConverge}, there exists constants $C_2, C_3>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(I_2>\varepsilon/2)\leq C_2 \exp[-C_3 (n \varepsilon^2)/\{1+(\kappa\tau)^2\}].$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $I_2$ by Theorem 6

nodes.name: Combine the two bounds
nodes.statement: Combining the bounds for $I_1$ and $I_2$ gives \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\beta})-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})>\varepsilon\Big) &\leq 2\exp(-C_1 n \varepsilon)+C_2 \exp\Big(-\frac{C_3 n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big)\\ &\leq C_4\exp\Big(-\frac{C_5 n \varepsilon^2}{1+(\kappa\tau)^2}\Big) \end{align*} for some constants $C_i>0$. This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:ModRiskDiffConverge}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two bounds

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5
nodes.statement: Consider \begin{align*} \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})-R(f^\ast, \beta^\ast) &= \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta}) - \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*) + \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*) - R(f^*, \beta^*)\\ &\leq \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*) - R(f^*, \beta^*), \end{align*} where the last inequality follows since $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\leq \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*)$ by the definition of $\widetilde f$, $\widetilde \beta$. Let $z_{i}:=|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta^\ast-\left<\Phi(x_i),f^\ast\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^2$, then $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f^\ast, \beta^\ast)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n} z_{i}$ is the average of i.i.d. random variables with $\mathbb{E}z_i=R(f^\ast, \beta^\ast)$ by definition of expected risk. Since $|z_i|\leq4(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{2}$, by Hoeffding's inequality $$ \mathbb{P}(| \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f^*, \beta^*)-R(f^*, \beta^*)|>\varepsilon)=\mathbb{P}\Big(\Big|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n} (z_{i}-\mathbb{E}z_i)\Big|>\varepsilon \Big)\leq 2\exp \Big(-\frac{n \varepsilon^2}{16(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}} \Big). $$
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to deviation of the modified empirical risk at $(f^*,\beta^*)$ by optimality, then apply Hoeffding's inequality to bounded i.i.d. losses.

nodes.name: Reduce to deviation at $(f^*,\beta^*)$
nodes.statement: Consider \begin{align*} \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})-R(f^\ast, \beta^\ast) &= \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta}) - \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*) + \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*) - R(f^*, \beta^*)\\ &\leq \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*) - R(f^*, \beta^*), \end{align*} where the last inequality follows since $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(\widetilde{f}, \widetilde{\beta})\leq \widetilde R_{emp}(f^*, \beta^*)$ by the definition of $\widetilde f$, $\widetilde \beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to deviation at $(f^*,\beta^*)$

nodes.name: Write the risk as an average of i.i.d. losses
nodes.statement: Let $z_{i}:=|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta^\ast-\left<\Phi(x_i),f^\ast\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^2$, then $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f^\ast, \beta^\ast)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n} z_{i}$ is the average of i.i.d. random variables with $\mathbb{E}z_i=R(f^\ast, \beta^\ast)$ by definition of expected risk.
nodes.statement_short: Write the risk as an average of i.i.d. losses

nodes.name: Apply Hoeffding's inequality
nodes.statement: Since $|z_i|\leq4(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{2}$, by Hoeffding's inequality $$ \mathbb{P}(| \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f^*, \beta^*)-R(f^*, \beta^*)|>\varepsilon)=\mathbb{P}\Big(\Big|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n} (z_{i}-\mathbb{E}z_i)\Big|>\varepsilon \Big)\leq 2\exp \Big(-\frac{n \varepsilon^2}{16(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}} \Big). $$
nodes.statement_short: Apply Hoeffding's inequality

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.statement: By definition of $R_{\text{emp}}(f)$ and $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))$, \begin{align*} R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))&=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2} - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta(f)-\left<\Phi(x_i), f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}\\ &=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\overline{Y\theta^*}-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}, f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}. \end{align*} Expanding the squares and cancelling equal terms yields \begin{align*} &R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))\\ &\quad = \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Big\{(y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta)^{2} - (y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}- 2y_{i}^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}-2\overline{Y\theta^*}\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}+2y_{i}^{\top}\theta^*\overline{Y\theta^*} -(\overline{Y\theta^*})^{2}\Big\}\\ &\quad = \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Big\{(y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta)^{2} - (y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}\Big\}- \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Big\{2y_{i}^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big\} + (\overline{Y\theta^*})^2\\ &\quad = I_1 + I_2(f) + I_3, \end{align*} where $I_1$ and $I_3$ are independent of $f$. By the union bound and de Morgan's law, $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau}|R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))|>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\Big(|I_1|>\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau}|I_2(f)|>\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big(|I_3|>\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big). $$ We bound each probability separately. Since $y_i\in \mathbb{R}^2$ is an indicator vector of class membership for sample $i$, using the definition of $\widehat \theta$ and $\theta^*$ \[ |I_1|=\bigg|\frac{1}{n}\sum\Big\{(y_i^{\top}\widehat\theta)^{2}-(y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}\Big\}\big|\leq \max_i|(y_i^{\top}\widehat\theta)^{2}-(y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}| = \max\Big(|n_1/n_2-\pi_1/\pi_2|,|n_2/n_1-\pi_2/\pi_1|\Big). \] By Lemma~\ref{lem:OptScoreSupNormBound}, there exist $C_1, C_2>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(|I_1|>\varepsilon/3)\leq C_1\exp(-C_2 n \varepsilon^2)$. By H{\'o}lder's and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities \begin{align*} |I_2(f)|&= \bigg|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}2y_i^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\bigg|\\ &\leq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} 2|y_i^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)|\cdot|\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|\\ &\leq 2 \|\widehat \theta-\theta^*\|_{\infty}\max_i|\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|\\ &\leq 2 \max\Big(|\sqrt{n_1/n_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2}|,|\sqrt{n_2/n_1}-\sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}|\Big)\max_i\|\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\,\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &\leq 4\max\Big(|\sqrt{n_1/n_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2}|,|\sqrt{n_2/n_1}-\sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}|\Big) \kappa\tau, \end{align*} where we used Assumption~\ref{assump:KernBound} in the last inequality. Since the upper bound does not depend on $f$, the same bound holds for $\sup_{f\in\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}|I_2(f)|$. Combining the bound with Lemma~\ref{lem:OptScoreSupNormBound} gives for some $C_3, C_4>0$ $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}|I_2(f)|>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\bigg(\max\Big(|\sqrt{n_1/n_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2}|,|\sqrt{n_2/n_1}-\sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}|>\frac{\varepsilon}{4\kappa \tau}\Big) \leq C_3\exp(-C_4 \frac{n \varepsilon^2}{(\kappa\tau)^2}). $$ By Lemma~\ref{lem:ytheta}, there exists $C_5>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(|I_3|>\varepsilon/3)\leq 2 \exp(-C_5 n \varepsilon)$. Combining the bounds for $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ gives \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}}| R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))|>\varepsilon\Big) &\leq C_1\exp(-C_2 n \varepsilon^2)+C_3\exp(-C_4 \frac{n \varepsilon^2}{(\kappa\tau)^2})+2 \exp(-C_5 n \varepsilon)\\ &\leq C_6\exp\Big(-C_7 \frac{n \varepsilon^2}{1 + (\kappa\tau)^2}\Big) \end{align*} for some $C_6, C_7>0$. This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:DifferenceRiskSupConverge}.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the squared losses into three terms; bound score terms by Lemmas 6 and 7 and the $f$-dependent term by Hoelder, Cauchy-Schwarz and Assumption 2.

nodes.name: Write the difference of risks
nodes.statement: By definition of $R_{\text{emp}}(f)$ and $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))$, \begin{align*} R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))&=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2} - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta(f)-\left<\Phi(x_i), f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}\\ &=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\overline{Y\theta^*}-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}, f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write the difference of risks

nodes.name: Expand into $I_1+I_2(f)+I_3$
nodes.statement: Expanding the squares and cancelling equal terms yields \begin{align*} &R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))\\ &\quad = \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Big\{(y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta)^{2} - (y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}- 2y_{i}^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}-2\overline{Y\theta^*}\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}+2y_{i}^{\top}\theta^*\overline{Y\theta^*} -(\overline{Y\theta^*})^{2}\Big\}\\ &\quad = \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Big\{(y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta)^{2} - (y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}\Big\}- \frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Big\{2y_{i}^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big\} + (\overline{Y\theta^*})^2\\ &\quad = I_1 + I_2(f) + I_3, \end{align*} where $I_1$ and $I_3$ are independent of $f$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand into $I_1+I_2(f)+I_3$

nodes.name: Union bound over three terms
nodes.statement: By the union bound and de Morgan's law, $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau}|R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))|>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\Big(|I_1|>\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau}|I_2(f)|>\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big)+\mathbb{P}\Big(|I_3|>\frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Big). $$ We bound each probability separately.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over three terms

nodes.name: Bound $|I_1|$ by score deviations
nodes.statement: Since $y_i\in \mathbb{R}^2$ is an indicator vector of class membership for sample $i$, using the definition of $\widehat \theta$ and $\theta^*$ \[ |I_1|=\bigg|\frac{1}{n}\sum\Big\{(y_i^{\top}\widehat\theta)^{2}-(y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}\Big\}\big|\leq \max_i|(y_i^{\top}\widehat\theta)^{2}-(y_i^{\top}\theta^*)^{2}| = \max\Big(|n_1/n_2-\pi_1/\pi_2|,|n_2/n_1-\pi_2/\pi_1|\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|I_1|$ by score deviations

nodes.name: Tail bound for $I_1$ by Lemma 6
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:OptScoreSupNormBound}, there exist $C_1, C_2>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(|I_1|>\varepsilon/3)\leq C_1\exp(-C_2 n \varepsilon^2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Tail bound for $I_1$ by Lemma 6

nodes.name: Bound $I_2(f)$ by Hoelder and Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: By H{\'o}lder's and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities \begin{align*} |I_2(f)|&= \bigg|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}2y_i^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\bigg|\\ &\leq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} 2|y_i^{\top}(\widehat \theta-\theta^*)|\cdot|\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|\\ &\leq 2 \|\widehat \theta-\theta^*\|_{\infty}\max_i|\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|\\ &\leq 2 \max\Big(|\sqrt{n_1/n_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2}|,|\sqrt{n_2/n_1}-\sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}|\Big)\max_i\|\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\,\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}}\\ &\leq 4\max\Big(|\sqrt{n_1/n_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2}|,|\sqrt{n_2/n_1}-\sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}|\Big) \kappa\tau, \end{align*} where we used Assumption~\ref{assump:KernBound} in the last inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $I_2(f)$ by Hoelder and Cauchy-Schwarz

nodes.name: Uniform tail bound for $I_2$ via Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Since the upper bound does not depend on $f$, the same bound holds for $\sup_{f\in\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}|I_2(f)|$. Combining the bound with Lemma~\ref{lem:OptScoreSupNormBound} gives for some $C_3, C_4>0$ $$ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{f\in\mathcal{H}_{\tau}}|I_2(f)|>\varepsilon\Big)\leq \mathbb{P}\bigg(\max\Big(|\sqrt{n_1/n_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1/\pi_2}|,|\sqrt{n_2/n_1}-\sqrt{\pi_2/\pi_1}|>\frac{\varepsilon}{4\kappa \tau}\Big) \leq C_3\exp(-C_4 \frac{n \varepsilon^2}{(\kappa\tau)^2}). $$
nodes.statement_short: Uniform tail bound for $I_2$ via Lemma 6

nodes.name: Tail bound for $I_3$ by Lemma 7
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:ytheta}, there exists $C_5>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(|I_3|>\varepsilon/3)\leq 2 \exp(-C_5 n \varepsilon)$.
nodes.statement_short: Tail bound for $I_3$ by Lemma 7

nodes.name: Combine the three bounds
nodes.statement: Combining the bounds for $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ gives \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\big(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}}| R_{\text{emp}}(f)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f, \beta(f))|>\varepsilon\Big) &\leq C_1\exp(-C_2 n \varepsilon^2)+C_3\exp(-C_4 \frac{n \varepsilon^2}{(\kappa\tau)^2})+2 \exp(-C_5 n \varepsilon)\\ &\leq C_6\exp\Big(-C_7 \frac{n \varepsilon^2}{1 + (\kappa\tau)^2}\Big) \end{align*} for some $C_6, C_7>0$. This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:DifferenceRiskSupConverge}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the three bounds

nodes.name: Zero solution for large lambda
nodes.statement: Consider minimizing $f(w) = 2^{-1}w^{\top} Q w-\beta^Tw +2^{-1}\lambda\|w\|_{1}$ with respect to $w\in \mathbb{R}^p$ with $w_i\in[-1,1]$, where $Q$ is positive semi-definite and $\lambda\geq 0$. If $\lambda\geq 2\|\beta\|_\infty$, then the minimizing $w$ is the zero vector.
conclusions: the minimizing $w$ is the zero vector
nodes.statement_short: If $\lambda\ge 2\|\beta\|_\infty$ the box-constrained lasso-type objective is minimized at $w=0$.
nodes.label: lem:lambdamax

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Consider $2^{-1}\lambda\|w\|_{1}-\beta^{\top}w=\sum_{i=1}^{p} (\lambda/2|w_i|-\beta_i w_i).$ If $\lambda \geq 2\|\beta\|_\infty$, this expression is non-negative for all $w\in \mathbb{R}^{p}$ and a minimum occurs at $w=0$. Since $Q$ is positive semi-definite, $w^{\top} \frac{1}{2} Q w$ is always non-negative with a minimum at $w=0$. It follows that for $\lambda \geq 2\|\beta\|_\infty$ the sum of these terms attains minimum at $w=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Both the penalized linear part and the PSD quadratic part are nonnegative and vanish at $w=0$.

nodes.name: Linear plus penalty part is nonnegative
nodes.statement: Consider $2^{-1}\lambda\|w\|_{1}-\beta^{\top}w=\sum_{i=1}^{p} (\lambda/2|w_i|-\beta_i w_i).$ If $\lambda \geq 2\|\beta\|_\infty$, this expression is non-negative for all $w\in \mathbb{R}^{p}$ and a minimum occurs at $w=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Linear plus penalty part is nonnegative

nodes.name: Quadratic part is nonnegative
nodes.statement: Since $Q$ is positive semi-definite, $w^{\top} \frac{1}{2} Q w$ is always non-negative with a minimum at $w=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic part is nonnegative

nodes.name: Sum is minimized at zero
nodes.statement: It follows that for $\lambda \geq 2\|\beta\|_\infty$ the sum of these terms attains minimum at $w=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum is minimized at zero

nodes.name: Operator norm bound for the KOS solution map
nodes.statement: Let $M = [(C\mathbf{K}C)^2+n\gamma (C\mathbf{K}C)]^{-}C\mathbf{K}C$, then $\|M\|_{\text{op}}\leq (n\gamma)^{-1}$.
nodes.label: lem:OpNormBound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: The kernel matrix $K$ is positive semi-definite since by the reproducing property for any $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^n$ $$ \alpha^{\top}\mathbf{K}\alpha=\left<\sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_{i}\Phi(x_i)\,,\, \sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}\Phi(x_i)\right>_{\mathcal{H}}=\Big\|\sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_{i}\Phi(x_i)\Big\|^{2}_{\mathcal{H}}\geq 0. $$ It follows that $C\mathbf{K}C$ is also positive semi-definite. Let $\{\lambda_{i}\}_{i=1}^{k}$ be the set of non-zero eigenvalues of $C\mathbf{K}C$, then $\{\lambda_{i}/(\lambda_{i}^{2}+n\gamma \lambda_{i})\}_{i=1}^{k}$ are the non-zero eigenvalues of $M=[(C\mathbf{K}C)^2+n\gamma (C\mathbf{K}C)]^{-}C\mathbf{K}C$. The function $t\mapsto t/(t^2+n\gamma t)$ is bounded above by $(n\gamma)^{-1}$ for $t>0$, hence $\|M\|_{\text{op}}\leq (n\gamma)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: $CKC$ is PSD by the reproducing property; eigenvalues of $M$ are $t/(t^2+n\gamma t)\le 1/(n\gamma)$.

nodes.name: Kernel matrix is PSD by the reproducing property
nodes.statement: The kernel matrix $K$ is positive semi-definite since by the reproducing property for any $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^n$ $$ \alpha^{\top}\mathbf{K}\alpha=\left<\sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_{i}\Phi(x_i)\,,\, \sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}\Phi(x_i)\right>_{\mathcal{H}}=\Big\|\sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_{i}\Phi(x_i)\Big\|^{2}_{\mathcal{H}}\geq 0. $$ It follows that $C\mathbf{K}C$ is also positive semi-definite.
nodes.statement_short: Kernel matrix is PSD by the reproducing property

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of $M$
nodes.statement: Let $\{\lambda_{i}\}_{i=1}^{k}$ be the set of non-zero eigenvalues of $C\mathbf{K}C$, then $\{\lambda_{i}/(\lambda_{i}^{2}+n\gamma \lambda_{i})\}_{i=1}^{k}$ are the non-zero eigenvalues of $M=[(C\mathbf{K}C)^2+n\gamma (C\mathbf{K}C)]^{-}C\mathbf{K}C$.
nodes.statement_short: Eigenvalues of $M$

nodes.name: Bound each eigenvalue
nodes.statement: The function $t\mapsto t/(t^2+n\gamma t)$ is bounded above by $(n\gamma)^{-1}$ for $t>0$, hence $\|M\|_{\text{op}}\leq (n\gamma)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound each eigenvalue

nodes.name: Norm bounds for the KOS minimizer
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma >0$. The minimizer $\widehat f$ in~\eqref{eq:RegKernOptScore} satisfies $\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq 1/\sqrt{\gamma}$. Additionally, if Assumption~\ref{assump:KernBound} holds for $\kappa >0$, then $\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq 2\kappa/\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: The KOS minimizer has RKHS norm at most $1/\sqrt\gamma$, and at most $2\kappa/\gamma$ under a bounded kernel.
nodes.label: lem:Bounds

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Comparing the value of objective function in~\eqref{eq:RegKernOptScore} at $f = \widehat f$ with the value at $f=0$ gives \begin{align*} \gamma\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}^{2}&\leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},\widehat{f}\,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big|^{2}+\gamma\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}^{2}\leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta|^{2}=1., \end{align*} where the last equality follows since $n^{-1}\widehat \theta Y^{\top}Y\widehat \theta = 1$. It follows that $\|\widehat f\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq 1/\sqrt{\gamma}$. On the other hand, since $\widehat{f} = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}(\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi})$, by the triangle inequality and Assumption~\ref{assump:KernBound} \begin{align*} \|\widehat{f}\|_\mathcal{H}= \Big\|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}(\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi})\Big\|_\mathcal{H}\leq \sum_{i=1}^{n}|\alpha_i|\|\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq \max_i \|\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\|_{\mathcal{H}} \|\alpha\|_1 &\leq 2\kappa \|\alpha\|_{1}\leq 2\kappa\sqrt{n}\|\alpha\|_{2}. \end{align*} Since $\alpha = \{(C\mathbf{K}C)^{2}+\gamma n C\mathbf{K}C\}^{-}C\mathbf{K}C Y\widehat \theta$, applying Lemma \ref{lem:OpNormBound} and using $\|Y\widehat \theta\|_2 = \sqrt{\widehat \theta Y^{\top}Y\widehat \theta} = \sqrt{n}$ gives \begin{align*} \|\alpha\|_{2}\leq \| \{(C\mathbf{K}C)^{2}+\gamma n C\mathbf{K}C\}^{-}C\mathbf{K}C\|_{\text{op}}\| Y\widehat \theta\|_{2} \leq\frac{\|Y\widehat \theta\|_{2}}{n\gamma} \leq \frac1{\sqrt{n}\gamma}. \end{align*} Combining the above two displays gives $\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq 2\kappa/\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the objective at $\widehat f$ and at $0$ for the first bound; triangle inequality plus Lemma 2 on the coefficients for the second.

nodes.name: Compare objective with $f=0$
nodes.statement: Comparing the value of objective function in~\eqref{eq:RegKernOptScore} at $f = \widehat f$ with the value at $f=0$ gives \begin{align*} \gamma\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}^{2}&\leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta-\left<\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi},\widehat{f}\,\right>_{\mathcal{H}}\Big|^{2}+\gamma\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}^{2}\leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\widehat \theta|^{2}=1., \end{align*} where the last equality follows since $n^{-1}\widehat \theta Y^{\top}Y\widehat \theta = 1$. It follows that $\|\widehat f\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq 1/\sqrt{\gamma}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare objective with $f=0$

nodes.name: Triangle inequality bound via $\|\alpha\|_2$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, since $\widehat{f} = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}(\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi})$, by the triangle inequality and Assumption~\ref{assump:KernBound} \begin{align*} \|\widehat{f}\|_\mathcal{H}= \Big\|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\alpha_{i}(\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi})\Big\|_\mathcal{H}\leq \sum_{i=1}^{n}|\alpha_i|\|\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq \max_i \|\Phi(x_i)-\overline{\Phi}\|_{\mathcal{H}} \|\alpha\|_1 &\leq 2\kappa \|\alpha\|_{1}\leq 2\kappa\sqrt{n}\|\alpha\|_{2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality bound via $\|\alpha\|_2$

nodes.name: Bound $\|\alpha\|_2$ by Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Since $\alpha = \{(C\mathbf{K}C)^{2}+\gamma n C\mathbf{K}C\}^{-}C\mathbf{K}C Y\widehat \theta$, applying Lemma \ref{lem:OpNormBound} and using $\|Y\widehat \theta\|_2 = \sqrt{\widehat \theta Y^{\top}Y\widehat \theta} = \sqrt{n}$ gives \begin{align*} \|\alpha\|_{2}\leq \| \{(C\mathbf{K}C)^{2}+\gamma n C\mathbf{K}C\}^{-}C\mathbf{K}C\|_{\text{op}}\| Y\widehat \theta\|_{2} \leq\frac{\|Y\widehat \theta\|_{2}}{n\gamma} \leq \frac1{\sqrt{n}\gamma}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|\alpha\|_2$ by Lemma 2

nodes.name: Combine the bounds
nodes.statement: Combining the above two displays gives $\|\widehat{f}\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq 2\kappa/\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the bounds

nodes.name: Reduction to epsilon-nets in symmetrization
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assump:ScoreBound} and \ref{assump:KernBound}, let $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$ and $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{j=n+1}^{2n}$ be two independent copies of i.i.d. data, and let $T_x$ be the empirical measure on their union. Let $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ be the modified empirical risk on $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$, and $\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ on $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{i=n+1}^{2n}$. Let $c=64(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty+\tau \kappa)$, and let $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ be the smallest $L^2(T_x)$ $\varepsilon/\sqrt{2}c$-net of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$, and let $\{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ be an $\varepsilon/c$-net of $I_\tau$. Then \begin{align*} \begin{split} \mathbb{P}\bigg(\sup_{\substack{f\in H_\tau\\ \beta\in I_\tau}}\{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{2} \bigg) \leq\mathbb{P}\bigg( \mathrm{maximize}_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}} \{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4} \bigg). \end{split} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The symmetrized supremum over the admissible class is controlled by the maximum over finite $\varepsilon$-nets at half the threshold.
assumptions: let $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$ and $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{j=n+1}^{2n}$ be two independent copies of i.i.d. data, and let $T_x$ be the empirical measure on their union. Let $\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ be the modified empirical risk on $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$, and $\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)$ on $\{(x_j, y_j)\}_{i=n+1}^{2n}$. Let $c=64(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty+\tau \kappa)$, and let $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ be the smallest $L^2(T_x)$ $\varepsilon/\sqrt{2}c$-net of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$, and let $\{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ be an $\varepsilon/c$-net of $I_\tau$
nodes.label: lem:EpsilonNetInSymmetrization

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Let $f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau$, $\beta\in I_\tau$ be such that $\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde R'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)>\varepsilon/2$. There exists $f_j\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ and $\beta_\ell\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ such that $\|f_j-f\|_{L^2(T_x)}<\varepsilon/\sqrt{2}c$ and $|\beta-\beta_\ell|<\varepsilon/c$. Applying Lemma \ref{lem:EpslnNetRestriction} gives \[ \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^{2}}<\frac{\varepsilon}{c}\quad\text{and}\quad \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=n+1}^{2n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^{2}}<\frac{\varepsilon}{c}. \] Applying Lemma \ref{lem:ClosenessOfEmpRisk} yields \[ |\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)|<8\frac{\varepsilon}{c}(\|\theta^*\|_{\infty} + \kappa \tau)= \frac{\varepsilon}{8}, \] and similarly $|\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)|< \varepsilon/8$. Therefore, $\widetilde R'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)>\varepsilon/2$ for some $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}$, $\beta \in I_{\tau}$ implies $ \widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)>\varepsilon/4 $ for some $f_j$ and $\beta_\ell$. Therefore, \[ \mathbb{P}\bigg(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau,\, \beta\in I_\tau}\{\widetilde R'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\bigg)\leq \mathbb{P}\bigg( \mathrm{maximize}_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}}\{\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4} \bigg). \]
nodes.statement_short: Approximate any violating $(f,\beta)$ by net points using Lemmas 9 and 8, losing at most $\varepsilon/4$.

nodes.name: Pick a violating pair and nearby net points
nodes.statement: Let $f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau$, $\beta\in I_\tau$ be such that $\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde R'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)>\varepsilon/2$. There exists $f_j\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ and $\beta_\ell\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ such that $\|f_j-f\|_{L^2(T_x)}<\varepsilon/\sqrt{2}c$ and $|\beta-\beta_\ell|<\varepsilon/c$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick a violating pair and nearby net points

nodes.name: Net property on each half-sample by Lemma 9
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma \ref{lem:EpslnNetRestriction} gives \[ \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^{2}}<\frac{\varepsilon}{c}\quad\text{and}\quad \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=n+1}^{2n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^{2}}<\frac{\varepsilon}{c}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Net property on each half-sample by Lemma 9

nodes.name: Risk closeness by Lemma 8
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma \ref{lem:ClosenessOfEmpRisk} yields \[ |\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)|<8\frac{\varepsilon}{c}(\|\theta^*\|_{\infty} + \kappa \tau)= \frac{\varepsilon}{8}, \] and similarly $|\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)|< \varepsilon/8$.
nodes.statement_short: Risk closeness by Lemma 8

nodes.name: Conclude the probability inequality
nodes.statement: Therefore, $\widetilde R'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)>\varepsilon/2$ for some $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}$, $\beta \in I_{\tau}$ implies $ \widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)>\varepsilon/4 $ for some $f_j$ and $\beta_\ell$. Therefore, \[ \mathbb{P}\bigg(\sup_{f\in \mathcal{H}_\tau,\, \beta\in I_\tau}\{\widetilde R'_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde R_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\bigg)\leq \mathbb{P}\bigg( \mathrm{maximize}_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}}\{\widetilde{R}'_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f_j, \beta_\ell)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4} \bigg). \]
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the probability inequality

nodes.name: Maximum over nets bound
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assump:ScoreBound}-\ref{assump:Separable}, let $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ and $\{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:EpsilonNetInSymmetrization}. There exist a constant $C_1>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$, \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\bigg( \mathrm{maximize}_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}} \{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4} \bigg)\leq \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon} \,\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big), \end{align*} where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp( C_1\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$.
nodes.statement_short: The symmetrized deviation maximized over the nets exceeds $\varepsilon/4$ with probability at most $\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon e^{-cn\varepsilon^2}$.
assumptions: let $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ and $\{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:EpsilonNetInSymmetrization}
conclusions: There exist a constant $C_1>0$ such that for all $\varepsilon>0$, \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\bigg( \mathrm{maximize}_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}} \{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4} \bigg)\leq \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon} \,\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big), \end{align*} where $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp( C_1\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$.
nodes.label: lem:MaxBound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma = \{\sigma_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be $i.i.d.$ Radamacher random variables, $\mathbb{P}(\sigma_i=1)=\mathbb{P}(\sigma_i=-1)=1/2$. Let $$ \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{\sigma}= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sigma_{i}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x_i),f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}, \quad \widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{'\sigma}= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=n+1}^{2n}\sigma_{i}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x_i),f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}. $$ Since $(y_i, x_i)$ and $(y_{n+i}, x_{n+i})$ are independent, and have the same distribution, the distribution of $\xi_{i}:=(|y_{i}^\top \theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x_{i}), f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}- |y_{n+i}^\top\theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x_{n+i}), f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2})$ is the same as distribution of $\sigma_i\xi_i$. Let $Z=\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{2n}$, then \[ \mathbb{P}_Z\bigg( \max_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\ \beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}} \{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}'(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4} \bigg)=\mathbb{P}_{Z,\sigma}\bigg(\max_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\\beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}}\{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{\sigma}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{'\sigma}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\bigg). \] Let $\mathcal{A}_{m,k}$ be the event $\mathcal{A}_{m,k} = \{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{\sigma}(f_m,\beta_k)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{'\sigma}(f_m,\beta_k) > \varepsilon/4\}$ for $m=1,\dots,M(Z)$; $k=1,\dots, K$; where $M(Z)$ emphasizes the dependence of $M$ on $Z$. Using properties of conditional expectation and union bound \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}_{Z,\sigma}\bigg(\max_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\\beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}}\{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{\sigma}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{'\sigma}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\bigg) &= \mathbb{P}_{Z, \sigma}(\cup_{m=1}^{M(Z)}\cup_{k=1}^K \mathcal{A}_{m,k})\\ &=\mathbb{E}_{Z}\left\{\mathbb{P}_{\sigma}(\cup_{m=1}^{M(Z)}\cup_{k=1}^K \mathcal{A}_{m,k}|Z)\right\}\\ &\leq \mathbb{E}_Z\left\{M(Z)K\mathbb{P}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{A}_{m,k}|Z)\right\}. \end{align*} For fixed $f_m$, $\beta_k$ and conditionally on $Z$, the terms $\psi_{i}:=\sigma_{i}(|y_{i}^\top \theta^*-\beta_{k}-\left<\Phi(x_{i}), f_{m}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}- |y_{n+i}^\top\theta^*-\beta_{k}-\left<\Phi(x_{n+i}), f_{m}\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2})$, $i=1, \dots, n$, are independent, mean-zero random variables with $|\psi_i|\leq 4(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{2}$. Applying Hoeffding's inequality gives $$ \mathbb{P}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{A}_{m,k}|Z) = \mathbb{P}_{\sigma}\Big(\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \psi_i > \varepsilon / 4\,\Big|\, Z\Big) \leq \exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big). $$ On the other hand, since $I_{\tau}$ is a one-dimensional sphere of radius $\|\theta^*\| + \kappa \tau$, $K$ is independent of the data and $K \leq 1 + 2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)/\varepsilon$. Combining this with the above two displays gives \begin{align*} &\mathbb{P}_{Z,\sigma}\bigg(\max_{\substack{f\in \{f_1, \dots, f_M\}\\\beta\in \{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}}}\{\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{\sigma}(f,\beta)-\widetilde{R}_{\text{emp}}^{'\sigma}(f,\beta)\}>\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\bigg)\\ &\leq \{1 + 2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)/\varepsilon\}\,\mathbb{E}_Z\{M(Z)\}\exp\Big(- \frac{n\varepsilon^2}{128(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa \tau)^{4}}\Big). \end{align*} Recall that $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ is the smallest $L^2(T_x)$ $\varepsilon/\sqrt{2}c$-net of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$, with $c=64(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty+\tau \kappa).$ By Lemma~\ref{lem:CoveringNum} \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_Z\{M(Z)\}\leq \sup_{Z=\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{2n}} M(Z)\leq\exp\bigg(\frac{C_1\tau^2}{ \varepsilon^2}\bigg) \end{equation} for some constant $C_1>0$. Setting $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}=\{1+2(\|\theta^*\|_\infty+\kappa\tau)/\varepsilon\} \exp( C_1\tau^2 \varepsilon^{-2})$ completes the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:MaxBound}.
nodes.statement_short: Rademacher symmetrization, union bound over net points with Hoeffding's inequality, and the covering-number bound of Lemma 10. The key step is Hoeffding conditionally on the data.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: We provide the proof for $n_1/n_2$, the proof for $n_2/n_1$ is analogous. The first inequality is equivalent to Lemma~1 in~\cite{gaynanova2017sparse}. nodes.name: Concentration of the mean population score
nodes.statement: Let Assumption \ref{assump:ScoreBound} be true. For all $\varepsilon>0$, we have $\mathbb{P}\big((\overline{Y\theta^*})^2>\varepsilon \big)\leq 2 \exp(- n \varepsilon/\|\theta^*\|_\infty)$.
nodes.label: lem:ytheta

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Let $z_i=y_i^{\top}\theta^*$, then $z_i$ are independent, $$ \mathbb{E}(z_i) = \mathbb{E}(y_i)^{\top}\theta^* = \pi_1\sqrt{\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1}} -\pi_2\sqrt{\frac{\pi_1}{\pi_2}}= \sqrt{\pi_1 \pi_2}-\sqrt{\pi_1 \pi_2}=0 $$ and $$ (\overline{Y\theta^*})^2 = (n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^ny_i^{\top}\theta^*)^2=(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nz_i)^2. $$ Since $|z_i|\leq \|\theta^*\|_{\infty}=\sqrt{\pi_{\max}/\pi_{\min}}$, by Hoeffding's inequality for $\varepsilon >0$ \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\Big(\Big|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nz_i\Big|^2>\varepsilon\Big) = \mathbb{P}\Big(\Big|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nz_i\Big|>\sqrt{\varepsilon}\Big)\leq 2\exp(-n \varepsilon/\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The population scores $y_i^\top\theta^*$ are bounded with mean zero; apply Hoeffding's inequality.

nodes.name: Closeness of modified empirical risks on nets
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{assump:ScoreBound} and \ref{assump:KernBound} be true, and suppose that $\{f_1, \dots, f_{M}\}$ is an $L^2 (T_{x})$ $\varepsilon$-net of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ and that $\{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_K\}$ be an $\varepsilon$-net of $I_\tau$. Then for any admissible $f$ and $\beta$, let $f_j$ and $\beta_\ell$ be members of the $\varepsilon$-nets so that $\|f-f_j\|_{L^2(T_x)}<\varepsilon$ and $|\beta-\beta_\ell|<\varepsilon$. Then \begin{equation} \left|\widetilde R_{emp}(f, \beta) - \widetilde R_{emp}(f_j, \beta_l)\right| \leq 8\varepsilon \Big(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty +\kappa\tau \Big). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement: By the reproducing property of $\mathcal{H}$, $\left<\Phi(x_i), f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}= f(x_i)$, and \begin{align*} &\Big|\widetilde R_{emp}(f, \beta) - \widetilde R_{emp}(f_j, \beta_l)\Big|\\ &=\Big|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x_i),f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta_\ell-\left<\Phi(x_i),f_j\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}\Big|\\ &=\Big|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-f(x_i)|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta_\ell-f_j(x_l)|^{2}\Big|\\ &=\Big|-2\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_i^{\top}\theta^*\{\beta+ f(x_i)-\beta_\ell-f_j(x_i)\}+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n[\{\beta+f(x_i)\}^2-\{\beta_\ell+f_j(x_i)\}^{2}]\Big| \\ &\leq \underbrace{2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\Big|\beta-\beta_l+\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\{f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)\}\Big|}_{I_1}+\underbrace{\Big|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n[\{\beta+f(x_i)\}^2-\{\beta_\ell+f_j(x_i)\}^{2}] \Big|}_{I_2}. \end{align*} Consider \begin{align*} I_1 = 2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\bigg|\beta-\beta_l+\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\{f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)\}\bigg|&\leq 2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\left\{|\beta -\beta_l|+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|\right\}\\ &\leq 2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\left\{\varepsilon + \Big[\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^2\Big]^{1/2}\right\}\\ &\leq 4\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\varepsilon, \end{align*} where we used $n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}[|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^2]^{1/2} \leq [n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^2]^{1/2}$ due to Jensen's inequality, and that $\|f-f_j\|_{L^2(T_x)}<\varepsilon$ and $|\beta-\beta_\ell|<\varepsilon$. Consider $I_2$. Using $a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b)$, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequalty, and Jensen's inequality, \begin{align*} I_2 &= \frac{1}{n}\bigg|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\{\beta+f(x_i)+\beta_\ell+f_j(x_i)\}\{\beta-\beta_\ell+f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)\}\bigg|\\ &\leq 2(\sup_{\beta\in I_\tau}|\beta|+ \sup_{x,f\in \mathcal{H_\tau}}|f(x)|)\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(|\beta-\beta_j|+|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|)\\ &\leq 2(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty +\kappa \tau+ \sup_{x,f\in \mathcal{H_\tau}}|\left< \Phi(x),f \right>_{\mathcal{H}}|)(\varepsilon+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|)\\ &\leq 2\bigg( \|\theta^\ast\|_\infty +\kappa \tau+\kappa \tau \bigg)\bigg(\varepsilon+\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^{2}}\bigg)\\ &=4\varepsilon \Big(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty +2\kappa \tau \Big). \end{align*} Combining the bounds for $I_1$ and $I_2$ completes the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:ClosenessOfEmpRisk}.
nodes.statement_short: Expand squares via the reproducing property; bound the linear term with Jensen and the quadratic term with $a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b)$ and Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Expand the difference into $I_1+I_2$
nodes.statement: By the reproducing property of $\mathcal{H}$, $\left<\Phi(x_i), f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}= f(x_i)$, and \begin{align*} &\Big|\widetilde R_{emp}(f, \beta) - \widetilde R_{emp}(f_j, \beta_l)\Big|\\ &=\Big|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-\left<\Phi(x_i),f\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta_\ell-\left<\Phi(x_i),f_j\right>_{\mathcal{H}}|^{2}\Big|\\ &=\Big|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta-f(x_i)|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|y_i^{\top}\theta^*-\beta_\ell-f_j(x_l)|^{2}\Big|\\ &=\Big|-2\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_i^{\top}\theta^*\{\beta+ f(x_i)-\beta_\ell-f_j(x_i)\}+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n[\{\beta+f(x_i)\}^2-\{\beta_\ell+f_j(x_i)\}^{2}]\Big| \\ &\leq \underbrace{2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\Big|\beta-\beta_l+\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\{f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)\}\Big|}_{I_1}+\underbrace{\Big|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n[\{\beta+f(x_i)\}^2-\{\beta_\ell+f_j(x_i)\}^{2}] \Big|}_{I_2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the difference into $I_1+I_2$

nodes.name: Bound $I_1$ via Jensen
nodes.statement: Consider \begin{align*} I_1 = 2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\bigg|\beta-\beta_l+\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\{f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)\}\bigg|&\leq 2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\left\{|\beta -\beta_l|+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|\right\}\\ &\leq 2\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\left\{\varepsilon + \Big[\frac1{n}\sum_{i=1}^n|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^2\Big]^{1/2}\right\}\\ &\leq 4\|\theta^*\|_{\infty}\varepsilon, \end{align*} where we used $n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}[|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^2]^{1/2} \leq [n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^2]^{1/2}$ due to Jensen's inequality, and that $\|f-f_j\|_{L^2(T_x)}<\varepsilon$ and $|\beta-\beta_\ell|<\varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $I_1$ via Jensen

nodes.name: Bound $I_2$ via Cauchy-Schwarz and Jensen
nodes.statement: Consider $I_2$. Using $a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b)$, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequalty, and Jensen's inequality, \begin{align*} I_2 &= \frac{1}{n}\bigg|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\{\beta+f(x_i)+\beta_\ell+f_j(x_i)\}\{\beta-\beta_\ell+f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)\}\bigg|\\ &\leq 2(\sup_{\beta\in I_\tau}|\beta|+ \sup_{x,f\in \mathcal{H_\tau}}|f(x)|)\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(|\beta-\beta_j|+|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|)\\ &\leq 2(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty +\kappa \tau+ \sup_{x,f\in \mathcal{H_\tau}}|\left< \Phi(x),f \right>_{\mathcal{H}}|)(\varepsilon+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|)\\ &\leq 2\bigg( \|\theta^\ast\|_\infty +\kappa \tau+\kappa \tau \bigg)\bigg(\varepsilon+\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)-f_j(x_i)|^{2}}\bigg)\\ &=4\varepsilon \Big(\|\theta^\ast\|_\infty +2\kappa \tau \Big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $I_2$ via Cauchy-Schwarz and Jensen

nodes.name: Add the two bounds
nodes.statement: Combining the bounds for $I_1$ and $I_2$ completes the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:ClosenessOfEmpRisk}.

nodes.name: Net restriction to half-sample
nodes.statement: Let $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{2n}$ be the data, and consider an $L^{2}(T_x)$ $\varepsilon$-net $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$. Then $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ is an $\sqrt{2}\varepsilon$-net with respect to the empirical measure on half of the data $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$.
nodes.statement_short: An $\varepsilon$-net in $L^2$ of the full double sample is a $\sqrt2\varepsilon$-net for either half.
conclusions: Then $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ is an $\sqrt{2}\varepsilon$-net with respect to the empirical measure on half of the data $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$
nodes.label: lem:EpslnNetRestriction

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement: Since $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ is $\varepsilon$-net with respect to $\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^{2n}$, for any $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\tau}$, there exists $f_j$ such that \[ \sqrt{\frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|f(x_i) - f_j(x_i)|^{2}}<\varepsilon. \] If $\frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|f(x_i) - f_j(x_i)|^{2}=0$, then $\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i) - f_j(x_i)|^{2}=0$. Otherwise \begin{align*} \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i) - f_j(x_i)|^{2}}&= \sqrt{\frac{2n}{2n}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i) - f_j(x_i)|^{2} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|f(x_i) - f_j(x_i)|^{2}}{\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|f(x_i)- f_j(x_i)|^2}}\\ &=\sqrt{\frac{2n}{n} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}|f(x_i)- f_j(x_i)|^{2}}{\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|f(x_i)- f_j(x_i)|^{2}}}\, \sqrt{\frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|f(x_i)- f_j(x_i)|^2}< \sqrt{2}\varepsilon, \end{align*} hence $\{f_1, \dots, f_M\}$ is $\sqrt{2}\varepsilon$-net with respect to $\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the half-sample average with the full-sample average; the ratio of sums is at most one.

nodes.name: Covering number bound for RKHS balls
nodes.statement: Let Assumption \ref{assump:Separable} be true, and Let $M(Z)$ be the size of an $L^2(T_x)$ $\varepsilon$-covering number of $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ with data $Z=\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$. There exists a $C>0$ independent of $n$, such that \begin{equation} \sup_{Z=\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}}M(Z)\leq \exp\bigg( \frac{ C\tau^2}{\varepsilon^2}\bigg). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The $L^2(T_x)$ covering number of the RKHS ball of radius $\tau$ is at most $\exp(C\tau^2/\varepsilon^2)$.
